1100: of uncertain affinity; the tongue; by implication, a language (specially, one naturally unacquired):--tongue.
1101: from γλῶσσα and the base of κόσμος; properly, a case (to keep mouthpieces of wind-instruments in) i.e. (by extension) a casket or (specially) purse:--bag.
1102: by variation for a derivative from (to tease cloth); a cloth-dresser:--fuller.
1103: from the same as γενέσια; legitimate (of birth), i.e. genuine:--own, sincerity, true.
1104: adverb from γνήσιος; genuinely, i.e. really:--naturally.
1105: akin to νέφος; gloom (as of a storm):--blackness.
1106: from γινώσκω; cognition, i.e. (subjectively) opinion, or (objectively) resolve (counsel, consent, etc.):--advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will.
1107: from a derivative of γινώσκω; to make known; subjectively, to know:--certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot.
1108: from γινώσκω; knowing (the act), i.e. (by implication) knowledge:--knowledge, science.
1110: from γινώσκω; well-known:--acquaintance, (which may be) known, notable.
1114: from (to wail); properly, a wizard (as muttering spells), i.e. (by implication) an imposter:--seducer.
1115: of Chaldee origin (compare גֻּלְגֹּלֶת); the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near Jerusalem:--Golgotha.
1116: of Hebrew origin (עֲמֹרָה); Gomorrha (i.e. Amorah), a place near the Dead Sea:--Gomorrha.
1117: from γέμω; a load (as filling), i.e. (specially) a cargo, or (by extension) wares:--burden, merchandise.
1118: from the base of γίνομαι; a parent:--parent.
1120: from a compound of γόνυ and the alternate of πίπτω; to fall on the knee:--bow the knee, kneel down.
1121: from γράφω; a writing, i.e. a letter, note, epistle, book, etc.; plural learning:--bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written.
1122: from γράμμα. a writer, i.e. (professionally) scribe or secretary:--scribe, town-clerk.
1124: from γράφω; a document, i.e. holy Writ (or its contents or a statement in it):--scripture.
1125: a primary verb; to "grave", especially to write; figuratively, to describe:--describe, write(-ing, -ten).
1126: from (an old woman) and εἶδος; crone-like, i.e. silly:--old wives'.
1127: from ἐγείρω; to keep awake, i.e. watch (literally or figuratively):--be vigilant, wake, (be) watch(-ful).
1128: from γυμνός; to practise naked (in the games), i.e. train (figuratively):--exercise.
1130: from a derivative of γυμνός; to strip, i.e. (reflexively) go poorly clad:--be naked.
1131: of uncertain affinity; nude (absolute or relative, literal or figurative):--naked.
1133: a diminutive from γυνή; a little (i.e. foolish) woman:--silly woman.
1135: probably from the base of γίνομαι; a woman; specially, a wife:--wife, woman.
1136: of Hebrew origin (גּוֹג); Gog, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist:--Gog.
1137: probably akin to γόνυ; an angle:--corner, quarter.
1138: of Hebrew origin (דָּוִד); Dabid (i.e. David), the Israelite king:--David.
1139: middle voice from δαίμων; to be exercised by a dæmon:--have a (be vexed with, be possessed with) devil(-s).
1140: neuter of a derivative of δαίμων; a dæmonic being; by extension a deity:--devil, god.
1142: from (to distribute fortunes); a dæmon or supernatural spirit (of a bad nature):--devil.
1143: a prolonged form of a primary root; to bite, i.e. (figuratively) thwart:--bite.
1145: from δάκρυ; to shed tears:--weep. Compare κλαίω.
1148: probably of Chaldee origin; Dalmanutha, a place in Palestine:--Dalmanutha.
1149: probably of foreign derivation; Dalmatia, a region of Europe:--Dalmatia.
1150: a variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to tame:--tame.
1151: probably from the base of δαμάζω; a heifer (as tame):--heifer.
1152: probably from the base of δαμάζω; perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian woman:--Damaris.
1153: from Δαμασκός; a Damascene or inhabitant of Damascus:--Damascene.
1154: of Hebrew origin (דַּמֶּשֶׂק); Damascus, a city of Syria:--Damascus.
1155: from δάνειον; to loan on interest; reflexively, to borrow:--borrow, lend.
1156: from (a gift); probably akin to the base of δίδωμι; a loan:--debt.
1158: of Hebrew origin (דָנִיֵּאל); Daniel, an Israelite:--Daniel.
1159: from δαπάνη; to expend, i.e. (in a good sense) to incur cost, or (in a bad one) to waste:--be at charges, consume, spend.
1161: a primary particle (adversative or continuative); but, and, etc.:--also, and, but, moreover, now (often unexpressed in English).
1162: from δέομαι; a petition:--prayer, request, supplication.
1163: 3rd person singular active present of δέω; also deon deh-on'; neuter active participle of the same; both used impersonally; it is (was, etc.) necessary (as binding):--behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be) need(-ful), ought, should.
1164: from the base of δεικνύω; a specimen (as shown):--example.
1165: from δεῖγμα; to exhibit:--make a shew.
1166: a prolonged form of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to show (literally or figuratively):--shew.
1168: from δειλία; to be timid:--be afraid.
1170: probably from the same as δεινῶς (through the idea of forgetting the name as fearful, i.e. strange); so and so (when the person is not specified):--such a man.
1171: adverb from a derivative of the same as δειλός; terribly, i.e. excessively:--grievously, vehemently.
1172: from δεῖπνον; to dine, i.e. take the principle (or evening) meal:--sup (X -er).
1173: from the same as δαπάνη; dinner, i.e. the chief meal (usually in the evening):--feast, supper.
1174: the compound of a derivative of the base of δειλός and δαίμων; more religious than others:--too superstitious.
1175: from the same as δεισιδαιμονέστερος; religion:--superstition.
1177: from δέκα and δύο; two and ten, i.e. twelve:--twelve.
1178: from δέκα and πέντε; ten and five, i.e. fifteen:--fifteen.
1179: from δέκα and πόλις; the ten-city region; the Decapolis, a district in Syria:--Decapolis.
1180: from δέκα and τέσσαρες; ten and four, i.e. fourteen:--fourteen.
1181: feminine of δέκατος; a tenth, i.e. as a percentage or (technically) tithe:--tenth (part), tithe.
1183: from δεκάτη; to tithe, i.e. to give or take a tenth:--pay (receive) tithes.
1185: from the base of δόλος; to entrap, i.e. (figuratively) delude:--allure, beguile, entice.
1187: from δεξιός and λαμβάνω; a guardsman (as if taking the right) or light-armed soldier:--spearman.
1188: from δέχομαι; the right side or (feminine) hand (as that which usually takes):--right (hand, side).
1189: middle voice of δέω; to beg (as binding oneself), i.e. petition:--beseech, pray (to), make request. Compare πυνθάνομαι.
1190: from Δέρβη; a Derbæan or inhabitant of Derbe:--of Derbe.
1191: of foreign origin; Derbe, a place in Asia Minor:--Derbe.
1193: from δέρμα; made of hide:--leathern, of a skin.
1194: a primary verb; properly, to flay, i.e. (by implication) to scourge, or (by analogy) to thrash:--beat, smite.
1195: from a (presumed) derivative of δεσμέω; to be a binder (captor), i.e. to enchain (a prisoner), to tie on (a load):-- bind.
1196: from δεσμόν; to tie, i.e. shackle:--bind.
1198: from δεσμόν; a captive (as bound):--in bonds, prisoner.
1199: neuter and masculine respectively from δέω; a band, i.e. ligament (of the body) or shackle (of a prisoner); figuratively, an impediment or disability:--band, bond, chain, string.
